perf.summary: Recurse only into the smaller partition and loop on the larger to bound stack depth to O(log q).
perf.currentCost: Two unconditional recursive calls QuickSort(left,j) and QuickSort(i,right). Worst-case (already-sorted / adversarial) input gives O(q) recursion depth, risking stack overflow for large q and adding call overhead Burst cannot elide.
perf.proposedChange: Convert to a hybrid: after partitioning, recurse into the smaller side and tail-loop (while-loop reassigning left/right) on the larger side. Guarantees recursion depth <= log2(q). Optionally cut to insertion sort for ranges < ~16.
perf.rationale: Bounds stack to O(log q) regardless of input, eliminating worst-case deep recursion and halving call-frame overhead; preserves identical ordering.
perf.risk: Pure refactor of the same partition scheme — output order unchanged. Must keep the parallel arrays (q,l,r,b) swapped together exactly as now.

perf.summary: The 'queries'/q array (parallel to l,r,b) is permuted by Swap but never read inside the sort; confirm it carries the query id payload, otherwise it is dead work.
perf.currentCost: Swap permutes q[i]/q[j] on every swap (one extra load/store/temp per swap) but Less and QuickSort never read q. If q holds query ids that callers need reordered alongside l/r/b, this is necessary; if not, it is pure overhead per swap.
perf.proposedChange: If q is the id payload meant to be reordered with the keys, keep it but document that contract clearly. If it is unused, drop the q parameter and the q[] swap to remove one quarter of the swap cost.
perf.rationale: Either eliminates ~25% of per-swap memory traffic in the sort, or clarifies a load-bearing-but-unobvious data dependency. Sorts do many swaps in the hot path.
perf.risk: Removing q changes the public Run signature and would break callers relying on reordered ids — only do this after confirming q is unused downstream. Keeping it has no correctness risk.

perf.summary: Branchless distinct-count update: derive the increment from the pre-increment value instead of an if.
perf.currentCost: if (freq[val] == 0) (*curDistinct)++; then freq[val]++ — a data-dependent branch per element in the hottest inner loop of Mo's traversal (called O((n+q)*n^{2/3}) times). Mispredicts are common because add/remove order is irregular.
perf.proposedChange: int f = freq[val]; *curDistinct += (f == 0) ? 1 : 0; freq[val] = f + 1; — or use the comparison result directly: *curDistinct += (int)(f == 0). Symmetrically for RemoveInt: freq[val] = f - 1 then *curDistinct -= (int)((f - 1) == 0). Lets the JIT/Burst emit a setcc instead of a branch.
perf.rationale: Removes a frequently-mispredicted branch from the innermost Mo loop, converting it to a branchless conditional add; this loop dominates total runtime.
perf.risk: Semantics identical (the (f==0)?1:0 add equals the conditional increment). Must read freq[val] once into a local to avoid an extra load and to keep the pre/post values consistent. No overflow concern for realistic frequencies.
